histamine.note: Liberator; also a true allergen for some (separate from histamine).

effects.note: Small trials — including one in people with chronic insomnia symptoms and one in elite athletes — found that two kiwis eaten nightly for several weeks shortened time to fall asleep and improved sleep efficiency. The mechanism looks more like serotonin and antioxidant content than melatonin itself: one trial found no rise in urinary melatonin despite the better sleep. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.

A meta-analysis of five randomised trials found kiwifruit measurably improved bowel movement frequency; one crossover trial had three kiwis a day beating a standard psyllium supplement outright (6.3 vs. 4.5 bowel movements a week). The actinidin enzyme and sorbitol content are the leading explanations, distinct from the fruit's sleep-aid mechanism above. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.
